name: TMAG5110B2AQDBVRQ1
title: 2D dual-channel high-sensitivity Hall-effect latch, automotive
summary: TMAG5110-Q1 and TMAG5111-Q1 hold two Hall-effect latches on two axes 90° apart (XY, ZX or ZY), so one SOT-23 gives quadrature signals from a rotating magnet. TMAG5110-Q1 brings out each latch on its own open-drain output; TMAG5111-Q1 turns them into speed and direction outputs. It runs from 2.5 V to 38 V, with 1.4 mT or 3 mT typical operate points and 40 kHz bandwidth, and is AEC-Q100 grade 1. TMAG5110B2AQDBVRQ1 is the ZX, 1.4 mT, independent-output version with pinout A.

notes: Part number code (TMAG511 o a s v Q DBV R Q1): o is 0 for independent latch outputs, 1 for speed and direction; a is A (XY), B (ZX) or C (ZY); s is 2 (1.4 mT) or 4 (3 mT); v is the pinout, A with VCC on pin 1, R with OUT2 on pin 1; Q is -40 °C to 125 °C; DBV is the 5-pin SOT-23; R is a 3000-unit large reel; Q1 marks the automotive grade and no suffix the catalog grade.
Catalog-grade versions without the Q1 suffix are TMAG5110 and TMAG5111.
All are active, in production, RoHS yes, SN lead finish. TMAG5110C2RQDBVRQ1 (pinout R) is preview information, not production data.

operation.text: Two chopper-stabilised Hall channels, each with its own amplifier and threshold comparator, share one die behind an internal regulator. One channel uses a planar element (Z, normal to the package top) and the others vertical elements (X, Y, in the package plane). Option A pairs X with Y, B pairs Z with X, and C pairs Z with Y. Because the two sensed axes sit 90° apart, the two channels see quadrature components of one rotating field, so their outputs are in quadrature regardless of magnet alignment or pole pitch.

Each open-drain output follows its own channel as a latch: it pulls low once the field on that axis rises past BOP (south pole) and releases high once it falls below BRP (north pole); between the two it holds its state. Alternating north and south poles are needed to toggle it.
The two latch results are combined inside: OUT1 gives a speed pulse train and OUT2 a level that reports the direction of rotation, so the host needs no quadrature decoding.
Each axis reads a south pole approaching from its sensitive direction as a positive field; a north pole from that direction, or a south pole from the opposite one, reads negative.

The field is strongest at the outer edge of a ring magnet, which gives the most freedom in air gap and sensitivity choice. XY parts sit in the plane of the magnet, facing it or beside it. ZX parts sit under the magnet or face it with the package front. ZY parts sit under the magnet in another orientation or face it with the package side. On the side face of the magnet the field is far weaker and the allowed distance shrinks; the high-sensitivity option helps there, and that position suits designs where the sensor must stay inside the magnet diameter. Any of these can be turned 180° about Z.

Once VCC passes 2.5 V the part takes tON to start, then tPD to set its outputs. On TMAG5110-Q1 pinout A the outputs are high during tPD, then go low if the field is above BOP. On TMAG5110-Q1 pinout R the outputs are low during tPD and stay low while the field sits between BRP and BOP, until BRP is crossed. On TMAG5111-Q1 OUT1 goes low and OUT2 goes high during tPD; afterwards the states depend on magnet position, rotation sense and variant.

The Hall signal is sampled every tPD and averaged between samples; the output changes when the average crosses BOP or BRP. Since the field and the sampling are not synchronised, the delay varies: about half a period at best (crossing just before mid-period), one period typically, and up to a further whole period at worst (crossing just after mid-period). After the delay, the output edge itself takes tF falling or tR rising.

The supply-current figure used for derating is 17 mA maximum. Self-heating limits the supply voltage at high ambient temperature: the derating curve gives the highest VCC for each ambient, following the maximum-supply-voltage equation.
Survives a continuous reverse supply down to –20 V and transients up to 40 V. Outputs are short-circuit protected and current limited.
AEC-Q100 qualified: temperature grade 1 (–40 °C to 125 °C ambient), HBM ESD classification H3A, CDM ESD classification C6. Functional-safety capable, with documentation for safety system design.

At the sensor, the magnet's flux density must exceed the maximum BOP and BRP limits of the magnetic characteristics, with extra margin for mechanical tolerance, temperature and magnet variation. Magnet fields generally fall as temperature rises.

A ring magnet on the shaft with the sensor nearby gives pulses as it turns, the host taking OUT1 and OUT2 on GPIO inputs beside the motor driver. Each channel runs to full speed independently. Bandwidth should exceed twice the pole rate: 22 500 RPM with 8 poles is 3000 poles per second, and the 40 kHz typical bandwidth is over thirteen times that. A magnet barely above BOP also cuts the top speed, since the field spends less time above the threshold. The radial and tangential field components give the two quadrature signals.
A ceramic decoupling capacitor of 0.01 µF or more sits close to the part, on the 2.5 V to 38 V DC supply.
Fields pass through non-ferromagnetic materials, including plastic and aluminium housings and the PCB, so the magnet may sit outside an enclosure or behind the board.
